subject: sperm whale
title: A Drone Caught Sperm Whales Headbutting, and It Wasn't the Big Males

scenes.text: Whalers swore sperm whales rammed with their heads. Nobody had filmed it.
In 1820, a sperm whale reportedly sank the whaleship Essex with two head-on strikes.
For two centuries, there was no video of these whales headbutting each other.
Then drones over the Azores and the Balearic Islands caught it, between 2020 and 2022.
The surprise: it wasn't giant bulls fighting. It was young whales, not yet adults.
Why they do it is still a mystery. But the old whalers weren't making it up.

description:
Drones have filmed sperm whales headbutting each other for the first time.
The footage from the Azores and Balearic Islands, published in Marine Mammal Science, showed sub-adult whales doing it, not the large males scientists expected.
Why do you think young whales headbutt?
first_comment: Some scientists doubt headbutting is common, because the whale's head holds the machinery it uses to make its clicks. Would you want to be in a boat near one?
